fields.hero_prompt: Build a salon landing page that saves every signup to a database I own.

faq_plan.q: What is a salon landing page?
How do I create a salon landing page?

plan.angle: The top 10 for salon landing page is design galleries and template lists (Figma, Behance, Dribbble, Embeddable, Nicepage) plus two booking-strategy guides: they show what a salon page looks like, never what happens after the request button. This page shows four salon types (a hair color studio, a nail studio, a brow and lash studio, a barbershop), each page built around one booking moment with the request form, the rule or alert behind it, and the database row it lands in. The spa landing page is a sibling and stays out of the headings; the booking form itself belongs to the Form hub and is never a heading here.
tab_stories: Copperline Color Studio takes $25 off a first color visit and ends the request form on a time window; of 52 requests this month, 33 picked a weekend and 19 picked a weekday, each saved as a row the front desk books from.
Juniper Nail Studio holds seats for groups: Imogen Vale holds 3 seats for Friday at 5:30 pm from her phone, and each seat lands as its own row under one contact.

Alder Lash Co. books by its fill rule: a fill requested more than 4 weeks after the last appointment books as the $120 full set instead of the $45 fill, and the page applies the rule before the calendar fills wrong.

Fadewell Barbershop runs its walk-in list on the page: a visitor joins from the sidewalk, sees a 40 minutes quoted wait, and every open chair posts to the shop's #front-of-house Slack channel with Dario Vance up next.
openers: Copperline Color Studio sells one visit
A group books differently than one client
Alder Lash Co. prices by the calendar
Walk-ins hate standing in a doorway
Pick the one visit the page sells
Price the work where the visitor reads it
Name the person behind the chair
Mark the page up as a local business
heading_shapes: The $25 first-visit offer asks for a window, not a slot (the offer, then what it asks instead)
Three seats held from one phone (the quantity held, then the device)
The calendar decides fill or full set (who decides, then the two outcomes)
Every open chair posts to the shop (the recurring event, then where it lands)
claims_to_source: schema.org lists HairSalon as a LocalBusiness type (under HealthAndBeautyBusiness)
Google's structured data guidance: use the most specific LocalBusiness sub-type possible
